subject: AcmePayments: prioritize model-affinity + routing SLO for launch
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.example.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: AcmePayments: prioritize model-affinity + routing SLO for launch

Team —

Quick ask from the field. AcmePayments is tightening their launch requirements for a payments fraud feature they plan to ship in ~8 weeks. They’ve made a strong commercial commitment (see deal id ACME-2026-EXP-47) but require two runtime guarantees before they go live: 1) a way to pin their tenant to a model variant / execution path (so inference outputs remain consistent for compliance evals) and 2) a routing SLO that keeps 95th% token latency under 250ms for their traffic regionally (east-us) during business hours.

Why this matters: Acme will be our first enterprise financial customer in this segment and the ARR upside is material (~$1.2M ARR in year 1). They will not accept a launch without these guarantees in writing. They are flexible on whether it’s called “pinning” or an “affinity policy” as long as behavior is deterministic and we can attest to it.

What I need from product & eng: a short feasibility note + effort estimate (spike vs full work), suggested acceptance criteria for the canary, and whether we can commit to a scoped canary (limited QPS, documented fallback) within 2 weeks. I’ve attached a one-pager from Acme and a rough buyer ask doc.

Can we align on a plan by EOD tomorrow? If we can’t meet that cadence, I’ll need wording for the customer on timelines so Legal/Sales Ops can communicate expectations.

Thanks —
Vanessa
VP, West Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acmepay-requirements-onepager.pdf (pdf), MAP-ProdSpec-v2.docx (docx)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AcmePayments: prioritize model-affinity + routing SLO for launch

Vanessa —

Thanks for the context and the one-pager. High level thoughts from Product: we can likely deliver an MVP that satisfies their requirement with a scoped approach, but there are trade-offs to call out up front.

Proposal (MVP):
- Implement a "soft-affinity" policy at routing: prefer the pinned model variant when capacity permits, with explicit documented fallback to a compatible variant if capacity is constrained.
- Expose tenant-level configuration (API + metadata) so we can show the customer which variant was used for each request (auditability).
- Define canary acceptance criteria: 7 days of 99% deterministic responses on a 1000 prompt sample (customer-provided) and latency 95p < 250ms under the defined QPS cap.

Open questions / risks:
- True hard pinning (no fallback) requires changes to autoscaler and capacity guarantees (Dedicated lanes / reservation) — that’s larger scope.
- Caching and KV-residency behavior will be critical for latency; we’ll need engineering input on size of warm cache and memory/eviction implications.
- We need to instrument traceids and sampling to prove determinism for their auditors.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Engineering spike (2w) to validate feasibility and produce an impact matrix.
2) Define canary window and QPS cap with Sales Ops + Customer.
3) If spike is green, we scope the MVP into a 3-sprint implementation.

Markus / Jasmine — can you confirm spike capacity and any showstopper risks you foresee?

— Priyom
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.example.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AcmePayments: prioritize model-affinity + routing SLO for launch

Vanessa / Priyom —

Engineering read: spike makes sense and we can estimate after the spike. Quick notes from infra perspective:

Technical sketch for the spike (2w):
- Prototype a routing policy that tags requests by tenant and preferred-variant header; add a policy layer that prefers pinned host pools and records the decision in the request trace.
- Measure KV cache warmup time and eviction rate for a synthetic tenant traffic pattern (we’ll need a 24h replay from Acme).
- Validate autoscaler interactions: ensure burst capacity won’t silently reassign pinned traffic to other pools.

Potential blockers:
- If they require hard-affinity (no fallback during any degradation), we need a dedicated reservation or explicit SLA with capacity guarantees — that’s non-trivial and could require a Dedicated commitment or a new billing path.
- Observability: proving determinism for an auditor requires request/response diffs plus stored prompt versions; storage cost needs estimating.

Estimate (very rough, post-spike):
- Spike: 2w (engineer x2, infra x1)
- MVP implementation: 3-4 sprints (includes QA and canary infra)
- Hard-affinity + legal SLA: additional 4-6 sprints and capacity/product contract work

I’ll attach a short impact CSV with resource-hours and a rough timeline. If Sales can accept the soft-affinity + documented fallback for an initial canary we can move fast.

Markus
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Attachments: affinity-impact-estimates.csv

From: Mike Hansen <mike.hansen@acme-pay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
Cc: AcmePayments Legal <legal@acme-pay.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: AcmePayments: prioritize model-affinity + routing SLO for launch

Vanessa / Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We understand the technical trade-offs and would be willing to accept a scoped canary that uses soft-affinity (preferred-variant with documented fallback) as long as:
1) We get a statement of expected behavior during fallback (what will change in outputs).
2) Canary runs at limited QPS (we propose 10% of expected production traffic for 14 days).
3) You provide a stored sample set and determinism report we can use for our compliance checks.

If those conditions are met we can sign the initial commitment and plan to expand once the canary metrics are validated. I’ve looped in Legal to align contract language around the canary.

Best,
Mike Hansen
Director, Product — Fraud Prevention
AcmePayments
